chapterNote: The second half of the acrostic begun in Psalm 9, and the complaint that the thanksgiving did not settle. Why do You stand far off? Why hide in the very times of trouble when Psalm 9 called You a stronghold? Then comes perhaps the Old Testament's fullest portrait of the practical atheist — not a man who argues there is no God, but one who lives as if there were none. His nose is in the air; 'no God' is the sum of his thinking; his ways hold up; he snorts at his rivals. He tells himself he will never be shaken, that God has forgotten, that God has hidden His face and will never see, that God will not call him to account. Meanwhile his mouth is full of cursing and deceit, and he crouches like a lion by the villages to drag the helpless off in his net. The psalm's turn is one word: You have seen. God looks at trouble and grief precisely in order to take them into His hand; the helpless can leave himself with Him; He has been the orphan's helper. So the prayer asks for the arm of the wicked to be broken and his wickedness audited to the last entry, and rests on the Song of the Sea: the LORD is King forever and ever. He has heard the desire of the afflicted; He will steady their heart and bend His ear, and mortal man, made of earth, will terrorize no more.

1.text: Why do You stand so far away, O LORD? Why keep Yourself hidden in the times of trouble?
1.amp: Why stand [amad] You afar off [rachoq], O LORD [YHWH]? why hide [alam] You Yourself in times [et] of trouble [tsarah]?
1.notes: lamah YHWH taamod be-rachoq (H3068, H5975, H7350): why do You STAND far off — the God who sat to judge in Psalm 9:4 now seems to be standing at a distance — talim le-ittot ba-tsarah (H5956, H6256, H6869): hidden for the times of trouble, the exact phrase Psalm 9:9 used for when He is a stronghold. Same words, opposite experience: that is the lament's whole complaint.

2.text: In his arrogance the wicked man hunts down the afflicted; let them be caught in the schemes they have devised.
2.amp: The wicked [rasha] in his pride ['In the pride of the wicked he doth persecute', gaavah, the KJV margin] does persecute the poor [ani — afflicted]: let them be taken [taphas — seized] in the devices [mezimmah — schemes] that [zu] they have imagined [chashab — devised].
2.notes: be-gaavat rasha yidlaq ani (H1346, H7563, H6041): in the pride of the wicked the afflicted is HUNTED — dalaq, hot pursuit, the word for a fire catching; yittaphesu bi-mezimmot zu chashabu (H8610, H4209, H2098, H2803): let them be caught in the very schemes they thought up — Psalm 9:15's net again. The prayer asks for nothing new, only that evil be allowed to complete its own circuit.

3.text: For the wicked man brags about the cravings of his soul; he blesses the greedy and spurns the LORD.
3.amp: For the wicked [rasha] boasts [halal] of his heart's ['soul's', nephesh, the KJV margin] desire [taavah — craving], and blesses [barak] the covetous ['the covetous blesseth himself, he abhorreth the LORD', batsa, the KJV margin], whom the LORD [YHWH] abhors [naats — spurns, despises].
3.notes: ki-hillel rasha al-taavat naphsho (H1984, H7563, H8378, H5315): the wicked PRAISES — halal, the hallelujah verb — his own soul's craving; u-botsea berekh niets YHWH (H1214, H1288, H5006, H3068): he blesses the profiteer, and spurns the LORD — or, as the margin reads it, the profiteer blesses himself and despises the LORD. Either way the liturgy is inverted: praise to appetite, blessing to greed, contempt to God.

4.text: The wicked man, his nose in the air, does not seek Him; 'There is no God' is the sum of all his thoughts.
4.amp: The wicked [rasha], through the pride [gobah — height] of his countenance [aph — nose, face], will not seek [darash] after God: God [Elohim] is not in all his thoughts ['all his thoughts are, There is no God', mezimmah, the KJV margin].
4.notes: rasha ke-gobah appo bal-yidrosh (H7563, H1363, H639, H1875): the wicked 'according to the height of his nose' — the Hebrew idiom for a lifted, sneering face — does not SEEK; en Elohim kol-mezimmotav (H430, H4209): 'no God' is all his scheming, the margin's reading — not a philosophical atheism but a practical one, the working assumption of a man who never looks up (cf. Psalm 14:1; Romans 3:11).

5.text: His ways prosper at all times; Your judgments are high above, out of his sight; as for all his foes, he snorts at them.
5.amp: His ways [derek] are always [et — at all times] grievous [chul — writhe, whirl; read by the WEB as 'prosper']; Your judgments [mishpat] are far above [marom — on high] out of his sight: as for all his enemies [tsarar — adversaries], he puffs [puach — snorts] at them.
5.notes: yachilu derakhav be-khol-et (H2342, H1870, H6256): his ways 'are strong' — chul, which the KJV took as 'grievous' and the WEB, with most readers, as 'prosper': the wicked man's road holds up at all times; marom mishpatekha mi-negdo (H4791, H4941): Your judgments are up on the heights, out of his line of sight — kol-tsorerav yaphiach bahem (H6887, H6315): all his adversaries he SNORTS at. Psalm 73:3-12's prosperous wicked in one verse.

6.text: He says in his heart, 'I will never be shaken; from generation to generation I will meet no harm.'
6.amp: He has said [amar] in his heart [leb], I shall not be moved [mot — shaken]: for I shall never ['unto generation and generation', dor, the KJV margin] be in adversity [ra — harm].
6.notes: amar be-libbo bal-emmot (H559, H3820, H4131): the wicked's creed, said inside — 'I shall not be moved' — the identical words the righteous say of themselves in Psalm 16:8 and 30:6, and the difference is the ground; le-dor va-dor asher lo-be-ra (H1755, H7451): for generation after generation, the margin's literal, no harm. He plans a dynasty of immunity.

7.text: His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and oppression; under his tongue are trouble and wickedness.
7.amp: His mouth [peh] is full [male] of cursing [alah] and deceit ['deceits', mirmah, the KJV margin] and fraud: under his tongue [lashon] is mischief [amal — trouble] and vanity ['iniquity', aven, the KJV margin].
7.notes: alah pihu male u-mirmot va-tokh (H423, H6310, H4390, H4820): his mouth full of alah — the oath-curse — and deceits and oppression; tachat leshono amal va-aven (H3956, H5999, H205): under his tongue, where a man keeps what he savors, trouble and aven, wickedness. Paul quotes the first half in Romans 3:14 for the whole race.

8.text: He sits in ambush by the villages; in hiding places he murders the innocent; his eyes stalk the helpless.
8.amp: He sits [yashab] in the lurking places of the villages [chatser]: in the secret places does he murder [harag] the innocent [naqi]: his eyes [ayin] are privily set ['hide themselves', tsaphan, the KJV margin] against the poor.
8.notes: yeshev be-marab chatserim (H3427, H2691): he SITS in ambush — the same yashab as the LORD's enthronement (Psalm 9:7, 11), now a robber's crouch by the villages. ba-mistarim yaharog naqi (H2026, H5355): in hiding he murders the innocent — enav le-chelekhah yitsponu (H5869, H6845): his eyes hide themselves, the margin's literal, watching the chelekhah, the hapless — a rare word used three times in this psalm and nowhere else.

9.text: He lurks in a hiding place like a lion in its thicket; he lurks to seize the afflicted; he seizes the afflicted, dragging him off in his net.
9.amp: He lies in wait [arab] in secret as a lion [aryeh] in his den [sok — thicket, covert]: he lies in wait [arab] to catch the poor [ani — afflicted]: he does catch the poor [ani], when he draws [mashak — drags] him into his net [resheth].
9.notes: yeerob ba-mistar ke-aryeh be-sukkoh (H693, H738, H5520): ambush like a lion in its sok, its covert — Psalm 17:12's picture; yeerob la-chatoph ani (H693, H6041): he lurks to SNATCH the afflicted — yachtoph ani be-moshkho be-rishto (H6041, H4900, H7568): snatches him, dragging him in his net. Lion, then hunter with a net: the predator changes shape but not appetite.

10.text: He crouches, he lies low, and the helpless fall by his strength.
10.amp: He crouches ['He breaketh himself', dakah, the KJV margin], and humbles [shachah — bows down] himself, that the poor may fall [naphal] by his strong ones ['into his strong parts', atsum, the KJV margin].
10.notes: yidkeh yashoach (H1794, H7817): he crushes down, he crouches — the lion flattening before the spring — ve-naphal ba-atsumav chelekhaim (H5307, H6099): and the hapless fall by his 'strong ones', his claws or his henchmen; the margin's 'strong parts' keeps the lion. The WEB reads the crushing as the victims': 'the helpless are crushed.'

11.text: He tells himself in his heart, 'God has forgotten; He has hidden His face and will never see it at all.'
11.amp: He has said [amar] in his heart [leb], God [El] has forgotten [shakach]: He hides [satar] His face [panim]; He will never [netsach] see [raah] it.
11.notes: amar be-libbo shakhach El (H559, H3820, H7911, H410): the second speech from the heart (v. 6): 'God has forgotten' — the exact thing Psalm 9:12 denied — histir panav bal-raah la-netsach (H5641, H6440, H7200, H5331): He has hidden His face, He will never see. The oppressor's theology is a doctrine of divine inattention; verse 14 answers it in one word.

12.text: Arise, O LORD! Lift up Your hand, O God; do not forget the afflicted ones.
12.amp: Arise [qum], O LORD [YHWH]; O God [El], lift up [nasa] Your hand [yad]: forget [shakach] not the humble ['afflicted', anav, the KJV margin].
12.notes: qumah YHWH El nesa yadekha (H6965, H3068, H410, H5375, H3027): rise, lift the hand — the answer to the wicked man's 'He has hidden His face' (v. 11); al-tishkach anavim (H7911, H6035): do not FORGET the afflicted — the psalmist takes the oppressor's word 'forgotten' (v. 11) and throws it into the prayer. Psalm 9:19's 'Arise' repeated.

13.text: Why does the wicked man treat God with contempt? He says in his heart, 'You will not call me to account.'
13.amp: Wherefore does the wicked [rasha] contemn [naats — spurn] God [Elohim]? he has said [amar] in his heart [leb], You will not require [darash — seek out, call to account] it.
13.notes: al-meh niets rasha Elohim (H5006, H7563, H430): WHY does the wicked spurn God — the lament's question turned from 'why do You stand far off' (v. 1) to 'why does he get away with it'; amar be-libbo lo tidrosh (H559, H3820, H1875): the third heart-speech: 'You will not seek it out' — darash, the word for God's blood-inquest in Psalm 9:12. He is betting against the audit.

14.text: You have seen it! For You take note of trouble and grief, to take it into Your own hand; the helpless leaves himself to You; You have been the helper of the fatherless.
14.amp: You have seen [raah] it; for You behold [nabat] mischief [amal — trouble] and spite [kaas — grief, vexation], to requite [natan — put] it with Your hand [yad]: the poor commits ['leaveth', azab, the KJV margin] himself unto You; You are the helper [azar] of the fatherless [yatom].
14.notes: raitah (H7200): 'You HAVE seen' — one word, and the wicked man's whole creed (vv. 11, 13) collapses. ki-attah amal va-khaas tabbit latet be-yadekha (H5999, H3708, H5027, H5414, H3027): You look at trouble and grief in order to take them into Your hand. alekha yaazob chelekhah (H5800): the hapless LEAVES himself to You, the margin's verb — abandonment as trust; yatom attah hayita ozer (H3490, H5826): You have been the orphan's helper — the same guardianship Exodus 22:22-24 states as a warning to the oppressor, this verse states as a comfort to the oppressed.

15.text: Break the arm of the wicked and evil man; call his wickedness to account until You find none left.
15.amp: Break [shabar — shatter] You the arm [zeroa] of the wicked [rasha] and the evil [ra] man: seek out [darash] his wickedness [resha] till You find [matsa] none [bal].
15.notes: shebor zeroa rasha (H7665, H2220, H7563): break the ARM — the limb that struck the villages — va-ra tidrosh-risho bal-timtsa (H7451, H1875, H7562, H1077, H4672): and the evil man: seek out his wickedness until You find none. The last of five darash-es across the pair (9:10, 12; 10:4, 13, 15), and the third aimed at God's own inquest: the account the wicked said would never be called is prayed down to the last entry.

16.text: The LORD reigns as King forever and ever; the nations have vanished from His land.
16.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is King [melek] for ever [olam] and ever [ad]: the heathen [goy — nations] are perished [abad] out of His land [eretz].
16.notes: YHWH melekh olam va-ed (H3068, H4428, H5769, H5703): the LORD is King forever and ever — an echo of the line the Song of the Sea ends on (Exodus 15:18, 'the LORD shall reign for ever and ever'), planted here as the answer to 'why do You stand far off'; abedu goyim me-artso (H6, H1471, H776): the nations have perished from HIS land — the perfect tense of faith, the future spoken as done.

17.text: LORD, You have heard the desire of the afflicted; You will steady their heart; You will bend Your ear to listen,
17.amp: LORD [YHWH], You have heard [shama] the desire [taavah] of the humble [anav — afflicted]: You will prepare ['establish', kun, the KJV margin] their heart [leb], You will cause Your ear [ozen] to hear [qashab — attend]:
17.notes: taavat anavim shamata YHWH (H8378, H6035, H8085, H3068): the DESIRE of the afflicted heard — taavah, the same craving-word the wicked boasted of in verse 3, now the humble's longing that God attends to; takhin libbam taqshib oznekha (H3559, H3820, H7181, H241): You will steady their heart — the margin's 'establish' — and make Your ear attend. God does two things: fixes the heart that prays, and listens to it.

18.text: to bring justice to the fatherless and the crushed, so that mortal man, who is of the earth, may terrorize no more.
18.amp: To judge [shaphat] the fatherless [yatom] and the oppressed [dak — crushed], that the man [enosh] of the earth [eretz] may no more [yasaph — add, do again] oppress.
18.notes: lishpot yatom va-dakh (H8199, H3490, H1790): to judge for the orphan and the crushed — the dak of Psalm 9:9 — bal-yosiph od la-arots enosh min-ha-aretz (H3254, H582, H776): that enosh, mortal man 'from the earth', may not go on terrifying — the margin's 'terrify' is the verb. The pair ends where Psalm 9 did: the tyrant is enosh, made of the ground he terrorizes, and the King is forever.
